batch_strategy: Structured failure repair with local condition-response curves, loading contrasts, calibration controls, and targeted structural exploration.

choices.reason: Adds an intermediate m204 loading point near the measured late-tail cases 45a1b11ae63f2dab2e48 and 73502a52708e4f9c2391, testing whether the predicted tail changes smoothly with ratio and loading.

hypotheses.content: Late-completion tails and onset shifts are strongly family- and condition-specific in polar, HBD-containing, or strongly adsorbing structures; broad model intervals are not reliably calibrated in either direction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Labels in several chemically distinct tail regimes can teach QGeoGNN when late completion is real, when broad predictions are overestimates, and how loading and solvent condition alter V1 and V2.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do nearby ratio and loading points reproduce the observed tails, or are the largest residuals isolated structure-specific events?

hypotheses.content: PE/EA ratio, loading amount, loading-solvent volume, and molecule structure interact locally, so condition response should be learned from matched molecule curves rather than a single global monotonic correction.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The selected m204, m173, m107, m103, m72, m32, and m81 groups provide matched local contrasts that can teach interaction terms and reduce interpolation errors across the catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the observed V1 and V2 shifts smooth along each local condition curve, or do functional-group environments produce reversals and threshold-like behavior?

hypotheses.content: Even moderate-width ordinary rows have uneven V2 calibration, with recurring completion bias that should be corrected alongside extreme-tail repair.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls prevent retraining from overfitting only to spectacular failures and help preserve accuracy across the large ordinary portion of the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do added ordinary controls reduce V2 bias without widening errors in the difficult late-elution regions?

hypotheses.content: Aromatic topology, fusion, halogen placement, and local functional-group environment can produce large retention residuals despite similar coarse descriptors, so structural anchors are needed around failure regions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Novel m58, m77, m63, m205, m213, and m147 labels test whether graph and descriptor representations transfer across underrepresented aromatic and HBD/HBA environments.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural changes preserve the local retention response, and which cause abrupt onset or tail shifts that require explicit graph-sensitive learning?

feedback_interpretation: The previous batch confirmed that large prediction widths are not calibrated uncertainty. The measured m173 and m204 cases 6802f0b28c5a0c7b4c2a and 73502a52708e4f9c2391 had V2 substantially later than predicted, while m11, m124, m103, and m3 cases such as 3e41bb94c582476b5b6a, 0e09f8144b025e4b5a8a, c98657e16e93ef4ede6b, and 1965d663b09320f566a5 showed substantial overprediction or onset error. The m32 and m81 outcomes support local response learning: onset was often comparatively stable while V2 changed materially with condition and loading. The m79 point was close, which weakens a universal failure claim and supports selecting matched curves. Ordinary controls m149, m52, m140, and m56 also showed uneven V2 calibration, so this batch retains moderate-width controls while expanding failure repair and structural coverage.
batch_rationale: The batch concentrates labels where previous feedback exposed distinct failure modes: m204, m173, m107, m103, m11, m95, m72, and m124 supply tail and onset repair across acids, oximes, polar esters, and aromatic systems. Their paired conditions test solvent-ratio response, loading volume, and local nonlinearity. m32, m81, m52, m149, and m140 provide calibration and response controls so retraining can improve difficult regions without sacrificing ordinary rows. Six structurally novel or underrepresented molecules add graph and functional-group coverage. Together these experiments cover high-impact residual regions, condition-response relationships, and representative Row-distribution structure rather than optimizing any individual chromatographic outcome.
